query: Earlier empirical-potential and first-principles studies primarily targeted phase-transition temperature, while other fusion properties remain difficult because they require free energies on both sides of the transition with vibrational entropy, anharmonicity, and electron–vibration coupling retained. Explicit ab initio free-energy evaluation is highly accurate but depends on costly molecular dynamics. TOR-TILD increased throughput for elemental and binary systems, yet slows substantially for multicomponent high-entropy systems. Under the constraint that the free energies of both solid and fluid states and the relevant entropy terms remain faithful, what single testable methodological hypothesis could substantially reduce the cost of obtaining fusion and high-temperature thermodynamic properties? State the proposed intervention and why it should work, predict its speed and fidelity relative to explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics workflows and TOR-TILD, define composition and temperature boundaries, cite supporting evidence from prior elemental or binary results, and specify a decisive benchmark of phase free energies and derived observables that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Integrating an ML-trained surrogate for ab initio free-energy evaluations that accurately captures both anharmonic and electron–vibration effects in solid and fluid phases will reduce computational cost while preserving the fidelity of phase free energies and derived melting properties.
generation.material_initial_state: Elemental or binary systems near their phase transition, where representative configurations defining solid and fluid states are available.
generation.intervention: Train a machine‐learning interatomic potential (e.g., based on Gaussian approximation potentials or neural network architectures) using a limited set of ab initio free-energy data for both phases, and then use this surrogate model within an enhanced sampling free-energy protocol.
generation.conditions: Tested in elemental and binary systems over a temperature window spanning approximately 20% below to 30% above the nominal fusion temperature. It is assumed to work under conditions where the fundamental binding and vibrational dynamics are well represented by the training dataset.
generation.structural_mediator: The ML potential learns the detailed interatomic force landscape, including effects of vibrational entropy, anharmonicity, and electron–vibration coupling, thereby mediating the transition from expensive AIMD evaluations to fast surrogate predictions.
generation.mechanism: By replacing many of the costly on-the-fly ab initio evaluations with rapid ML predictions—validated and periodically corrected against ab initio data—the method retains the accuracy of free energy and entropy estimates while dramatically cutting simulation time.
generation.predicted_outcome: The proposed workflow should achieve phase free energy accuracy comparable to explicit AIMD (error within ~5%) and determine fusion temperatures within a 2% error margin, while reducing computational time by at least an order of magnitude relative to full AIMD and offering a 2–3× speed improvement over TOR-TILD in binary systems.
generation.baseline: Comparisons will be made against full ab initio molecular dynamics and TOR-TILD free-energy evaluations in similar elemental and binary systems.
generation.boundary: This hypothesis is expected to be valid for systems up to binary compositions and within the stated temperature range. Its applicability to multicomponent, high-entropy systems remains uncertain due to the heightened complexity in capturing all relevant entropy contributions.
generation.uncertainty: The extent to which the ML potential can reliably capture electron–vibration coupling and anharmonic effects, especially near critical phase boundaries or in more complex multicomponent systems, remains uncertain until further testing.

falsification_experiment.design: Apply the ML-enhanced free-energy evaluation method to a series of well-characterized elemental and binary systems with existing benchmark data from ab initio MD and TOR-TILD. Obtain phase free energies and melting temperatures using the ML workflow and compare directly with those obtained using the benchmark methods.
measurements: Calculated free energies of solid and liquid phases
Quantification of vibrational entropy and anharmonic contributions
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the ML-enhanced method results in deviations greater than 5% in free energy and over 2% in fusion temperature when compared to the benchmarks, or if the entropy-related contributions are not faithfully reproduced, the hypothesis will be falsified.
